findings.title: enableSqlExpressions is a hard-coded `false` that ignores the feature flag
findings.body: `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions); if enabled { return false }; return false` returns false on every path. The `sqlExpressions` toggle is now a no-op: enabling it changes nothing. The double negation and duplicated `return false` suggest the logic was gutted from a real flag check, so a future reader may think the flag still gates something. It also dereferences `h.features` for no effect, so a reader built with nil features would panic on an SQL query. Since the feature is intentionally off, return the error directly and drop the pointless flag lookup. Alternatively, document that the flag is now inert and fix its registry description.

findings.title: User-facing error text "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is misleading
findings.body: SQL expressions were deliberately disabled for a security fix, and the feature flag still exists and is documented. Users who enable the flag now get "sqlExpressions is not implemented", which looks like a missing feature or a bug. The message should say the feature is disabled, preferably with a pointer to the CVE or advisory. The flag's registry description and docs still advertise SQL expressions and should be updated or marked as non-functional.

findings.title: Other SQL entry point reports a misleading error and is only blocked by the stub
findings.body: The disable check lives only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. `UnmarshalSQLCommand` and `NewSQLCommand` have no gate, so the legacy node-building path is blocked only because the stubbed `TablesList` returns "not implemented". That path then logs a Warn "invalid sql query", including the full user SQL, and returns "error reading SQL command" (`sql-invalid-sql`). Callers are told their SQL is invalid when the feature is disabled. Failing closed here is good, but the two entry points give inconsistent errors, and the security property depends on the stub rather than an explicit check. Put the disabled check in `NewSQLCommand` too, so all paths behave the same.

findings.title: No tests cover the new disabled behavior; existing SQL tests need updating
findings.body: The PR replaces the DuckDB-backed implementation with stubs that always return "not implemented", and adds a reader gate that always rejects SQL queries, with no tests. Nothing asserts that `QueryTypeSQL` is rejected, or that `NewSQLCommand`, `TablesList` and `Execute` fail closed. Any existing tests (for example in `pkg/expr/sql` and `pkg/expr`) that exercise successful SQL parsing or execution can no longer pass. They should be skipped or removed explicitly rather than left failing or silently untouched. A regression test for the security-relevant gate is also missing.
